agree.reason: The tone is candid, the partners commit to the same three days, and the stipend helps, so office-based staff will likely go along, but the eleven remote hires who live within two hours get no real reason to accept a three-day commute in place of the arrangement they say keeps them at the firm.

honest.reason: The note is careful about the junior-progression cause, but it claims as fact that the hospital bids were lost 'because of how we came across as a team', which goes beyond what the clients said, and it brings in an undecided 'Mondays and Fridays' question that the brief never raised.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are passed on as given: the note never works out that 15 of 46 is a third of the firm, that 11 remote hires face the full change without any phase-in, or what the 30% delay means in months or in fewer project leads.

right_comparison.reason: Staying fully remote is shown only through two lost bids and a single progression figure, with no sense of a trend or of what keeps happening if nothing changes, and the stipend and project-lead facts are not set against it.

qualification.reason: The six-month review has no date (it would fall around March 2028), no measure for success and no stated consequence, and 'before September' for the Monday/Friday decision is vague.

objections.reason: The note admits it is changing the terms the remote hires joined on and makes clear there are no further exceptions, but it does not speak to the long commutes of the eleven, people's reasons for staying, or the desk shortage in any concrete way.

fit.reason: It is a clear, one-page email with a subject line that points readers to Friday's meeting, as the brief asked.
